Every operative clause of v1.0.28 remains in force, unamended and unweakened: the HPO-ODS-W2-26 allocation, its branch binding, its three patterns, the two-path future registration surface, the closed world, the prohibitions and the CE-1 sequencing. purpose: Close the single authority gap that makes the HPO-ODS-W2-26 registration act, as authorized by v1.0.28, impossible to perform without violating v1.0.28's own narrowness clause. v1.0.28 declares the post-registration count 14 but never binds it to any operation, and never reaches the live-count guard that registering W2-26 is guaranteed to break. This addendum authorizes the atomic predecessor-demotion / live-count-promotion pair that resolves the deadlock, and authorizes nothing else.

THE_AUTHORITY_GAP.name: LIVE_COUNT_GUARD_TRANSFER
THE_AUTHORITY_GAP.statement: Registering HPO-ODS-W2-26 moves the live PROTECTED_GRANTS array from 13 rows to 14. Exactly one assertion in tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts compares a FROZEN artifact field against the LIVE array length. That assertion currently reads the v1.0.25 field PROTECTED_GRANTS_COUNT_AFTER_IMPLEMENTATION_REGISTERS_W2_25, whose frozen value is 13. After registration it evaluates 13 against 14 and FAILS. v1.0.28 neither anticipates this nor authorizes touching it.

GAP_MEASURED_NOT_ASSERTED.occurrence_disposition: Its own declaration, with value 14. It is never referenced by any other clause of v1.0.28 and is never bound to any future operation. The predecessor states the number and stops.
GAP_MEASURED_NOT_ASSERTED.occurrence_disposition_2: v1.0.28 never names the field whose assertion registration is guaranteed to break, and never names the live-count guard at all. The words 'demote', 'promote' and 'rebound' appear zero times in v1.0.28 in any casing.

THE_AUTHORITY_GAP.WHY_THE_PREDECESSOR_CANNOT_SIMPLY_BE_REA: v1.0.28 AUTHORIZED_FUTURE_REGISTRATION_SURFACE authorizes, on tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts, the count update from 13 to 14, the row-shape and duplicate additions, and the single absence-literal advance — and then closes the enumeration with 'NO existing control may be weakened, skipped, loosened to an inequality, or deleted. Additions, the count update, and the single absence-literal advance only.' The live-count guard is none of those three authorized operations: it is not the length assertion, not the Set-cardinality assertion, and not the absence literal. Worse, the ONLY correct repair — replacing a binding to the live array with a frozen literal — is on its face the 'weakening of an existing control' the same clause prohibits. A registering mission is therefore simultaneously GUARANTEED to break this control and NOT AUTHORIZED to repair it. That is a fail-closed deadlock, and closing it is the entire reason this successor exists.
THE_AUTHORITY_GAP.THE_THIRD_WAY_IS_PROHIBITED: Editing docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.25.json so that its field reads 14 would make the assertion pass. It is PROHIBITED. v1.0.25 is frozen, integrated, enumerated by the Controller under IMMUTABLE_BY_CONVENTION, and its figure is a true statement about the state that obtained when it was written. Changing it would corrupt the historical record to satisfy a present-tense guard. This prohibition is not novel: the surviving comment at the S1 demotion site in tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts already states it in the repository's own words — 'editing the artefacts to say 13 would corrupt the historical record'.

SEMANTIC_IDENTIFICATION_NOT_LINE_NUMBER.rule: The target is THE UNIQUE assertion in tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts whose RECEIVED expression is the v1.0.25 addendum field PROTECTED_GRANTS_COUNT_AFTER_IMPLEMENTATION_REGISTERS_W2_25 and whose EXPECTED argument is the bare expression PROTECTED_GRANTS.length. It is identified by that pairing and by nothing else.
SEMANTIC_IDENTIFICATION_NOT_LINE_NUMBER.why_not_a_line_number: Line numbers are not authority. The registration act itself adds rows to this file and moves every line below its insertion point, and any figure stated here would be stale before the implementer reached it. v1.0.28 already learned this and required re-measurement for the absence literal; the same discipline applies here.
SEMANTIC_IDENTIFICATION_NOT_LINE_NUMBER.DISAMBIGUATION_MEASURED: The expression PROTECTED_GRANTS.length occurs at EXACTLY TWO sites in this file at START_HEAD. The FIRST is the live registry-size assertion of the form `expect(PROTECTED_GRANTS.length).toBe(13)`, where the live array is the RECEIVED value and the literal is the EXPECTED value; that site is NOT this target and is governed by v1.0.28's already-authorized count update from 13 to 14. The SECOND is this target, where the operands are the other way round. The two are distinguished by which side the live array sits on, which is a property of the source and not of its position.
SEMANTIC_IDENTIFICATION_NOT_LINE_NUMBER.uniqueness_requirement: The implementer MUST re-measure at their own base and MUST confirm that exactly ONE site matches the rule. If zero or more than one site matches, that is a STOP: the file has changed in a way this authority did not anticipate, and the implementer must escalate rather than choose.

DEMOTE.required_result: The expected argument becomes the historically frozen literal 13. The assertion thereafter reads: the v1.0.25 field PROTECTED_GRANTS_COUNT_AFTER_IMPLEMENTATION_REGISTERS_W2_25 equals 13.
DEMOTE.literal_derivation: MEASURED, not chosen. docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.25.json PROTECTED_GRANTS_COUNT_AFTER_IMPLEMENTATION_REGISTERS_W2_25 holds the integer 13 at START_HEAD. The literal is the value the frozen artifact actually asserts — it is not the pre-registration live count that happens to share the number, and it must be re-derived from the artifact rather than copied from this sentence.
DEMOTE.exactness_is_unchanged: The demoted assertion remains an exact equality against an exact integer. Nothing is loosened to an inequality, skipped, or deleted. What changes is WHICH fact the assertion pins: it stops tracking the live array and starts pinning the historical claim of a frozen artifact, which is the only claim that artifact ever made.
DEMOTE.MEASURED_PRECEDENT: This exact operation has been performed once before in this exact file, and the record of it survives in place. When HPO-ODS-W2-25 was registered, the S1 guards were demoted to the historical literal 12 and the live binding moved to the newest registration. The surviving comment states the reasoning in full — that rebinding frozen artefacts to the live length 'would make two frozen authority artefacts appear to predict a count they never claimed', that editing the artefacts instead 'would corrupt the historical record', and that therefore 'the guard is demoted to the literal those artefacts actually assert, and the LIVE binding moves to the newest registration below. The exactness is unchanged.' This addendum authorizes the same operation one turn later and adds no new doctrine.

PROMOTE.required_result: After W2-26 is registered, the v1.0.28 field PROTECTED_GRANTS_COUNT_AFTER_A_FUTURE_MISSION_REGISTERS_W2_26 becomes THE ONE assertion bound to the live expression PROTECTED_GRANTS.length. It is the successor of the demoted guard and inherits its role exactly: a registry that grew by more or fewer than the one authorized entry fails here.
PROMOTE.reading_the_predecessor_artifact_is_an_a: The v1.0.28 JSON is not currently read by this test at START_HEAD. Reading it is an ADDITION to the file, which v1.0.28's own narrowness clause permits without further authority. This addendum notes it so the implementer does not mistake a necessary new read for an unauthorized widening.
PROMOTE.EXACTLY_ONE_LIVE_GUARD: BINDING. After the pair completes there must be EXACTLY ONE assertion in this file binding a frozen addendum field to the live expression PROTECTED_GRANTS.length, and it must be the v1.0.28 field. Two live-count guards is a defect, not extra safety: the older one would fail on the next registration for a reason the next lane did not cause, and the whole point of the demotion discipline is that only the NEWEST registry change holds the live binding.
PROMOTE.value_derivation: MEASURED. The integer 14 is read from the frozen v1.0.28 field, and it is also the arithmetic successor of the measured live count 13. Both derivations agree at START_HEAD. The implementer MUST re-derive both at their own base rather than inheriting 14 from this sentence, because the PROTECTED_GRANTS row count is a shared, globally-serialized resource that another lane can move; if the two derivations disagree, that is a STOP.

ATOMICITY.requirement: BINDING. DEMOTE and PROMOTE are ONE INDIVISIBLE registration act. Both MUST land in the SAME registration commit as the HPO-ODS-W2-26 row itself. Neither may be deferred to a follow-up commit, a follow-up PR, or a follow-up mission.
ATOMICITY.DEMOTE_WITHOUT_PROMOTE: PROHIBITED. The suite would be green and the repository would hold NO live-count guard at all. The registry could then grow, shrink or be silently reordered by any later lane with nothing to catch it. This is the more dangerous half precisely because it is the half that looks fine.
ATOMICITY.PROMOTE_WITHOUT_DEMOTE: PROHIBITED. The demoted assertion would still evaluate the frozen 13 against a live 14 and the suite would be red. The obvious local repairs are both prohibited elsewhere in this artifact — editing v1.0.25 corrupts frozen history, and deleting the assertion weakens an existing control — so this half leaves the registering mission with no authorized way forward.
ATOMICITY.why_atomicity_is_load_bearing_and_not_st: Each half, taken alone, produces a state that a later reader would reasonably mistake for a finished one: the first is green with no guard, the second is red with no authorized repair. Requiring the pair in one commit is what makes the transfer verifiable as a transfer — the count of live-count guards goes from one to one, never through zero and never through two.
ATOMICITY.verification: An auditor confirms atomicity by observing, in the SINGLE registration commit, that the demoted literal is present, that the promoted live binding is present, and that the number of assertions binding a frozen addendum field to PROTECTED_GRANTS.length is exactly one before and exactly one after.

CONTROLLER_40_RULE.why_the_two_axes_are_decoupled: The Controller's IMMUTABLE_BY_CONVENTION array governs which artifacts may not be edited and gates the allocation of the NEXT lineage ordinal. The PROTECTED_GRANTS registry governs which branch may touch which protected path. They are independent registries with independent controls. A missing Controller enumeration would let a later lane edit v1.0.29 without tripping the immutable guard — which is why it is required — but it does not and cannot prevent a grant from resolving. Conflating the two would stall CE-1 behind a bookkeeping step that has no bearing on it. This decoupling is the same one v1.0.28 records for the Controller39 precondition.
